correctness.rationale: For a strictly convex equiangular 8-gon with equal opposite-support distances, the central symmetral is the regular octagon by the original Konicer et al. equality characterization. Represent its opposite side lengths s±d_j, with d=(-[a-b]/sqrt2, a,-[a+b]/sqrt2,b). Two planar closure equations give this complete two-parameter representation; strict positivity of all eight sides is exactly |a|<s, |b|<s, |a|+|b|<sqrt2 s. Midpoint polygon W_j=(P_j+P_{j+4})/2 has edges d_j v_j, giving oriented area -(a²+b²)/4 by independent symbolic shoelace calculation. Also A(P)=2(1+sqrt2)s²-(a²+b²)/2; checked independent exact Q(sqrt2) symbolic vertex reconstruction, no reliance on numerical samples. On the compact closure of normalized feasible (u,v), u²+v² is maximized only at (1,sqrt2-1) and swapped; sign choices give eight boundary vertices; hence ratio rises to (sqrt2-1)/6, strictly below for positive side lengths and no attained 8-gon. Both strictness and limiting sequences follow by continuity. Domain excludes general CPPOS, smooth bodies and degenerate boundary polygons.

evidence: Konicer et al Theorem 4.7 has universal sup |A*(W)|/A(P)=1/4 over broad CPPOS; Theorem 4.4 says equal-area-isoperimetric cases have regular central symmetral. Neither determines constrained sharp ratio (sqrt2-1)/6.
The octagon optimizer falls on boundary of strict eight-positive-edge cone and is not a universal 1/4 extremizer.

value.rationale: The main 2026 CPPOS isoperimetric equality class is a canonical geometric subclass; finding its sharp octagonal caustic area fraction and all eight limiting shapes is a motivated exact constrained extremum, genuinely stronger within that class than the broad 1/4 inequality. The finite number of sides is not an arbitrary slice: eight is the first setting with the displayed two free unequal-opposite-edge parameters, yielding a complete clean classification.
